speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) by what date will the Ministry collect carbon tax payments for 2019 emissions; (b) by what date does the Ministry plan to publish the total amount of carbon tax payments collected for 2019 emissions; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider releasing a breakdown of revenue collected from each taxable facility when the data is available.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am just hoping we can publish that data of what each company is paying.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The public scrutiny on that, if you compare year by year, then the company's policy with regard on climate change will move much faster, if there is public scrutiny on that.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The intention behind the carbon tax is to provide an economy-wide price signal.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is not meant to put scrutiny on facilities or companies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, what we do, by publishing the data on an economy-wide basis, would be more useful for the Government and the public to know which sectors we should be concentrating on and how we are going to move from there.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we do not find it productive or correct to actually put any company under scrutiny because they pay their carbon tax or because they are compelled by the Act to do so.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, we know at least which industry is contributing more to carbon emissions in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But they account for about 80% of the carbon emissions in our economy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, even if you publish by facilities, you can actually do your Maths and make inferences on who is doing what, and I do not think that is what we want to get to.
